data.narrative:
Realta Fusion is a Series A–stage nuclear energy company that has raised $36M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 11 firms across the nuclear energy sector: 3 public companies (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers including Fuse Energy, Helion, Oklo, Valar Atomics, and X-Energy.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a valuation proxy, applies a 2.0x multiplier typical for Series A progression to next stage, implying $72M. Peer-median analysis across 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Valar Atomics ($6.0B, Series B), Nano Nuclear Energy ($808M, Seed), and Fuse Energy ($200M, Series A)—yields a median of $808M. The peer range spans $200M to $6.0B, reflecting high dispersion in the nuclear energy private market.

Triangulation across both methods supports a valuation range of $61M to $929M, with a median of $440M. The wide band reflects material uncertainty around stage-adjusted capital intensity versus peer multiples in an emerging, heterogeneous sector. Stage-progression yields conservative flooring; peer-median analysis pulls materially higher, anchored to Fuse Energy comparability at identical stage. Execution risk, technology differentiation, and capital efficiency relative to the broader peer set remain key drivers of value realization within this range.
